text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, executions followed one strict sequence: A26 → A27 → A28 in essentially every trace — about 99 in 100 of A26's outgoing transitions went to A27, about 99.5 in 100 of A27's went to A28, and A26 preceded A27, and A27 preceded A28, in about 199 of 200 traces. In the later window this sequence remains in only about 51 in 100 traces; in the other ~49, A26 leads instead to A32, A33 or A38 (roughly 17, 16 and 15 in 100 of its outgoing transitions respectively). [DIR001, DIR002, REL001, REL005]
- A32, A33 and A38 were not observed at all in the earlier window; in the later window each occurs in about 98–99 of 200 traces (~50%), positioned around the middle of the trace (median relative position ~0.5). [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- The new group and A27 behave as alternatives: after the change, A27 co-occurs with A32, A33 or A38 in at most about 0.5 in 100 traces, whereas before A27 was present in all traces and the group in none; A27 now appears in about 51 in 100 traces. [REL001, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- Ordering around the new group is consistent: A26 precedes each of A32, A33 and A38 in about 49 in 100 traces, and each of them precedes A28 in about 49 in 100. Within the group, members co-occur in ~49% of traces in both orders (e.g., A32 before A33 in ~23% and A33 before A32 in ~27%), so there is no fixed order among the three, and each can be the one handing over to A28. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- The distance from A26 to A28 shifted accordingly: before, A28 followed A26 two positions later in ~98% of traces; in the later window this holds in ~50%, while A28 follows four positions later in ~48% — consistent with three activities sitting between them. [LAG001]
- Minor: A27's outgoing transitions diversified slightly (to A28 from ~99.5% to ~96%, with small new edges to A09, A34 and A25 at ~1–2% each), and A26 gained a small edge to A23 (~0.5%). [DIR001, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural insertion: in the later window, about half of the executions replace the single step A27 between A26 and A28 with a group of three activities — A32, A33 and A38 — that run together in no fixed order between A26 and A28, while the original A26 → A27 → A28 path continues in the other half. This is shown directly by A26's outgoing transitions splitting roughly 50/50 between A27 and the group, the group's near-complete mutual exclusivity with A27, A26 consistently preceding and A28 consistently following the group, and the A26→A28 distance shifting from two to four positions in ~48% of traces. All items have empirical strength of about 0.995, and the 23 qualifying items far exceed the 0.35 expected by chance for 71 tested units. Limitations: the evidence cannot show whether the three activities are truly concurrent or merely unordered, and it cannot rule out that the later window mixes two coexisting variants — that is, the alternative branch may have existed before but gone unsampled in the 200 earlier traces rather than being newly added. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, LAG001]

Other differences: the small redirections at A27 (new edges to A09, A34 and A25 at ~1–2% each) and the small new edge A26 → A23 (~0.5%) are minor and are not part of the main hypothesis. [DIR001, DIR002]
